# Font licenses

Every `.woff2` in this folder is a redistribution of a Google Fonts family, licensed under the
**SIL Open Font License 1.1** (OFL-1.1). Each font now sits next to its own license file
(`<Family>.LICENSE.txt`) that carries the full license text, so the package no longer relies on
a link to Google Fonts for redistribution terms.

The license text is **not** the same file for every family: each upstream family directory has its
own `OFL.txt` with a family-specific copyright header, so the 20 license files were taken one by
one from `google/fonts` rather than copied from a single source. All 20 families are under the
`ofl/` directory upstream and all 20 declare `license: "OFL"` in their `METADATA.pb`. No family
here is Apache-2.0, UFL, or OFL-1.0.

## How a license file is laid out

Each `<Family>.LICENSE.txt` starts with a metadata header (family, bundled binary, font version,
copyright, license id, upstream URLs, retrieval date) and then contains the upstream license file
byte for byte:

```text
----- BEGIN VERBATIM UPSTREAM OFL.txt -----
<upstream OFL.txt, unmodified>
----- END VERBATIM UPSTREAM OFL.txt -----
```

Everything between the two markers is the upstream `OFL.txt` exactly as fetched from
`google/fonts` (branch `main`) on 2026-10-23. The sha256 values in the next table pin that text.
For 19 of the 20 files the marked block is byte-identical to the upstream file. For
`Montserrat.LICENSE.txt` the upstream `OFL.txt` has no trailing newline, so a single LF was added
to close the last line before the end marker; the license text itself is unchanged.

The hash covers exactly the bytes between the two markers. For 19 files that block is byte-identical
to the upstream `OFL.txt`; for `Montserrat.LICENSE.txt` the upstream file has no trailing newline,
so the block adds one LF and its hash differs from the upstream file's
(`8b7141c03fa4f8d44e6345d5d4931709290f0f67875e452e95ac1fd3a027802e`).

To re-check a license file against upstream:

```sh
# fetch the upstream text and compare it with the marked block
curl -sL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/google/fonts/main/ofl/<family>/OFL.txt -o /tmp/upstream.txt
sed -n '/BEGIN VERBATIM UPSTREAM OFL.txt/,/END VERBATIM UPSTREAM OFL.txt/p' <Family>.LICENSE.txt \
  | sed '1d;$d' > /tmp/embedded.txt
diff /tmp/upstream.txt /tmp/embedded.txt
```

## Copyright and version discrepancies

Checked family by family against the current upstream `google/fonts` release; these are the only
differences found.

- **Roboto** - the bundled binary is `Version 3.015`, its name table license URL is
  `https://openfontlicense.org`, and `google/fonts` keeps the family under `ofl/roboto` with an
  OFL-1.1 `OFL.txt`. The Apache-2.0 text belongs to the v2 series, whose sources live in
  `googlefonts/roboto-2` (that repository ships an "Apache License, Version 2.0" `LICENSE` file);
  the project this file was built from, `googlefonts/roboto-classic`, states "Both fonts and
  software found in this repo are all available under the OFL License v1.1". `google/fonts` has no
  `apache/roboto` directory (the contents API returns 404 for it), so no Apache text is shipped
  here.
- **Lato** - the bundled binary is `Version 1.104; Western+Polish opensource` (copyright 2010-2011),
  while the current upstream release is `Version 2.015` (copyright 2011-2015). Both are OFL-1.1 with
  Reserved Font Name "Lato", so the shipped upstream license text still governs, but the copyright
  line in the binary is the older one and is recorded in `Lato.LICENSE.txt`.
- **Bebas Neue** - the current upstream `OFL.txt` header reads "Copyright (c) 2010 by Dharma Type.",
  while the bundled binary (and the current upstream TTF) carry "Copyright 2019 The Bebas Neue
  Project Authors (https://github.com/dharmatype/Bebas-Neue)". Same OFL-1.1 text, different copyright
  attribution; both are recorded.
- **Inter** - upstream `OFL.txt` header reads "Copyright 2020 The Inter Project Authors"; the bundled
  binary carries "Copyright 2016 The Inter Project Authors (https://github.com/rsms/inter)". Same
  OFL-1.1 text.
- **Montserrat** - upstream `OFL.txt` header reads "Copyright 2024 The Montserrat.Git Project
  Authors (https://github.com/JulietaUla/Montserrat.git)"; the bundled binary carries "Copyright 2011
  The Montserrat Project Authors (https://github.com/JulietaUla/Montserrat)". Same OFL-1.1 text.
- **Playfair Display** - upstream `OFL.txt` header ends with Reserved Font Name "Playfair Display",
  the binary with "Playfair Display." (the full stop sits inside the quotes). Same OFL-1.1 text.
- **Abril Fatface** - the upstream `OFL.txt` header omits a repeated "Copyright (c) 2011," that is
  present in the binary's copyright string. Same holder, same OFL-1.1 text.
- **Righteous** - upstream `OFL.txt` header says "Reserved Font Names", the binary says "Reserved
  \rFont Name". Same OFL-1.1 text.

For the other 13 families the upstream `OFL.txt` header, the upstream release binary, and the
bundled binary agree on family name, PostScript name, version, and copyright line.

## Bundled fonts that are variable-font instances

Four bundled files are the default named instance of an upstream variable font: `DM-Sans.woff2`
("DM Sans 9pt"), `Montserrat.woff2` ("Montserrat Thin"), `Rubik.woff2` ("Rubik Light"), and
`Teko.woff2` ("Teko Light"). The family-level OFL-1.1 licence above covers each of them; the
versions recorded here (`Version 4.004`, `Version 9.000`, `Version 2.300`, `Version 2.000`)
are the upstream family versions the instances were taken from.

## Uncertainties

- The upstream `google/fonts` repository is a moving target: the `OFL.txt` files were read from
  branch `main` on 2026-10-23 and the recorded sha256 values pin exactly what was embedded. A later
  upstream edit will change the file at the recorded URL, so the sha256 table above, not the URL
  alone, is the authoritative reference for what this package ships.
- Seven families (Abril Fatface, Bebas Neue, Inter, Lato, Montserrat, Playfair Display, Righteous)
  have an upstream copyright header that differs from the copyright string inside the binary; both
  texts are kept (the binary wording in the table above, the upstream wording in the license file),
  and no attempt was made to reconcile them into a single "correct" attribution.
- The bundled binaries were compared against the current upstream release binaries. 19 of the 20
  match on family name, PostScript name, version, and copyright; Lato is the one older release
  described above.
